findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The nozzles on the soda machine were observed soiled. Discussed with PIC. PIC removed the nozzles and instructed a staff member to clean and sanitize them. Inspected reexamined the nozzles and they appeared cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer bucket was recorded at 0ppm at the start of the inspection. The sanitizer bucket was made during the inspection and tested at 200ppm QUAT from the dispenser at the triple sink. Ensure sanitizer buckets are readily available and regularly tested to ensure the efficacy of the sanitizer remains intact. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitizers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on device and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following areas were observed with an accumulation of dust/soil:
-The gaskets of the pizza prep cooler have an accumulation of food soils.
-The wire shelf above the prep table has an accumulation of dust/soils.
Ensure these surfaces are cleaned and sanitized to remove the current accumulation and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The lights in the kitchen and the air vents are observed with an accumulation of dust. Ensure the lights and air vents are cleaned to remove the current accumulation and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The soda nozzles in the self-service area are observed to have an accumulation of mold on the nozzles. The facility had a fresh set soaking in sanitizer water and are changing them out during today’s inspection. Ensure the soda nozzles are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The black fan in the kitchen and the fan cage of the display walk-in freezer are observed to have an accumulation of dust/debris. These items need to be cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. Facility is establishing a weekly cleaning policy for these items in order to maintain them clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-303.11: There is observed a lightbulb burnt out in the hood system above the fryer. Once items have cooled off either at the beginning or end of a shift, ensure this lightbulb is replaced.
6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: At the start of the inspection, the hand sink in the kitchen was observed to be out of paper towels. This was brought to the kitchen manager’s attention and the paper towels were restocked during the inspection. Ensure that hand sinks are always stocked and ready with the required items.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The black fan being used in the kitchen is observed to have an accumulation of dust/debris. Ensure this surface is cleaned in order for no potential contamination to take place. This cleaning should take place at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of dust/debris.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14:  The wiping cloths were observed to be stored outside of the sanitizer bucket. Ensure these cloths are placed into the chemical sanitizing bucket between uses to prevent contamination from the wiping cloth onto surfaces.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: The spatula in the pizza prep cooler was stored with food debris on it, but the debris was being blocked by the plastic barrier preventing it from causing cross contamination. Ensure utensils are stored in a manner to help prevent cross contamination of other food items.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-303.11: There are observed burnt out lightbulbs in the ventilation hoods above the conveyor oven. Ensure these bulbs are replaced in order to produce adequate lighting.
6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No proof of certified food protection manager on duty at the time of the inspection. Medium risk facilities are required to be under the operation of a CFM during operating hours--this changed when the FDA Food Code was adopted.
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1) Observed coffee maker spouts to be soiled. Wash, rinse and sanitize coffee maker spouts. 

2) Observed employee wash and rinse mixing bowl and place to air dry without sanitizing first. Quaternary ammonium sanitizer in the wall mounted unit is empty and there are no replacements on site at the time of the inspection. Facility does have bleach available but bleach does not have an EPA registration number on the label although it does say "kitchen sink" on the label. Facility will switch to this bleach in the meantime until they are able to supply an approved sanitizer. 

4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Equipment is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11  (P) After cleaning, utensils must be sanitized before use. Reference 4-702.11.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed the following items which exceed the 7 day date marking allowed in the pizza prep cooler: taco meat (10/9), beans (10/1), spinach dip (10/2), BBQ (9/27), turkey (10/7), roast beef (9/27), pork (9/29), corn (10/2). These items were discarded during the inspection. 

Observed half and half and iced coffee in the dispensers in the customer service area to not be date marked with the date of opening. Label on iced coffee box states to refrigerate after opening and follow local health codes once open. Date marking for these items will be checked on the follow up inspection on Monday.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed iced coffee and half and half spouts to be cut straight across rather than at the required 45 degree diagonal angle. Cut dispensing tube properly. 

Observed single service items to be stored out of the box and on the floor in the back storage area. This includes paper towels, toilet paper and boxes of cups. Store single service items at least 6" off the floor. 

4-502.13  (C) Bulk milk container dispensing tube not properly cut. The bulk milk dispensing tube shall be cut on the diagonal leaving no more than 1 inch protruding from the chilled dispenser. Reference 4-502.13.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles are stored incorrectly. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed prepared coffee filters stored open and accessible to the public in the self service area. Store coffee filters protected from potential contamination.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
No test strips were able to be located in the facility. They are using quaternary ammonium in the kitchen and are using bleach for the self service counters. Provide both quaternary ammonium and chlorine test strips for testing sanitizer concentration.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> No sanitizer was testing in the third compartment sink in the kitchen. Water was soiled and in need of being changed. Employee did not demonstrate a strong knowledge of how to prepare sanitizer and therefore, sanitizer was prepared during the inspection, showing the employee how to use test strips to test the concentration of the sanitizer. There was no sanitizer bucket prepared at the time of inspection either and there was an in use wiping cloth on the counter. Make sure employees are all trained on how to prepare sanitizer so that it tests at 200-400 ppm quaternary ammonium solution.
750-800b To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
No sanitizer bucket was prepared in the kitchen and there was a soiled wiping cloth stored on the counter. Prepare sanitizer buckets to 200-400 ppm quaternary ammonium solution and store wiping cloths in sanitizer in between use.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed pizza boxes stored underneath the three compartment sink and on the floor next to the mixer. Store single service items at least 6" off of the floor and do not store under plumbing.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Hand sink was blocked with a shirt at the beginning of the inspection. Shirt was later moved from the sink basin to the faucet handle area. Store shirt in an area where it is not blocking or interfering with proper hand washing.
750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a spray bottle of what was reported to be degreaser in the kitchen that was not labeled. Spray bottle was labeled during the inspection. Make sure all chemicals removed from their original container are labeled with the common name.
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Fan in the men's restroom is missing the cover. Replace cover on the fan.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Coffee maker was soiled with food accumulation. Clean coffee maker.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment:
Observed no covered waste can in the women's restroom. Provide a covered waste can.
750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed what appears to be slime mold on the ice flap of the main ice machine. Wash, rinse,and sanitizer food contact surface.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Milk was observed on the floor of the walk in cooler. Store milk 6 inches or higher off the floor.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed cups being used as scoops in the cheese and sausage of pizza prep table. Use scoops with a handle and store handle extended out of food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1)Observed a crack at the back right hand corner of the pizza prep cooler lid. Repair or replace lid. 2)Observed exposed wood on the shelves in pizza prep area holding cans and pizza sauce and shelf underneath microwave. Seal or paint shelves.
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
1)No paper towels at the hand sink by the ice machine. Provide paper towels. 2)Observed no covered waste can in women's restroom. Provide covered waste can.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Caulk at three compartment sink is wearing from the wall. Recaulk sink.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 17.830g  Obtain a test kit for checking the strength of the sanitizer in the spray bottles (chlorine sanitizer).  Mix the sanitizer so it is 100-150 parts per million chlorine.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Several packages of food were opened (bags open, boxes not closed) in the kitchen walk-in freezer.  Keep the bags and boxes closed or else move the food to closed food-grade containers

750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Plastic cups were used a scoops in food in the top of the prep cooler.  Replace the cups with scoops that have handles and keep the handles up out of the food.

750-280 To avoid unnecessary manual contact with food, suitable dispensing utensils shall be used by employees or provided to consumers who serve themselves..

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
There was no test kit for checking the strength of the chlorine sanitizer in the 3-pan sink and spray bottles used to sanitize food prep surfaces.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)   Obtain a test kit that will work with the chlorine sanitizer.  The sanitizer should be mixed to 50-100 ppm in the 3-pan sink and 100-15- ppm in the spray bottles.

750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
The inside of the cappuccino dispenser was soiled with cappuccino powder.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)   Clean and sanitize the inside of the dispenser.

750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The top of the filter pot below the 3-pan sink was soiled.  Clean the pot.

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
There were no soap and paper towels at the handsink in the kitchen near the pizza oven.   Provide soap and paper towels at the sink.

750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment:
The dumpster was missing some of its lids.  Contact your garbage hauler to have replacement lids put on the dumpster, or have the hauler provide you with a new dumpster.  Keep the lids closed at all times.

750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1.  The floor of the kitchen walk-in freezer was soiled.  Clean the floor.
2.  The floor under the ice machine (back toward the wall) was soiled.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)  Clean the floor.
3.  The floor drain and the area around it in the back electrical room was soiled.  Clean the drain and floor around it.
4.  There was a gap under the coving under the women's restroom sink.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)  Seal the gap.

750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Ceiling tiles over the self-service area were acoustic tiles.   Replace with tiles that are smooth, cleanable, and non-absorbent.

750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
There was no certified Food Service Sanitization Manager (FSSM) on duty.  Have a full time employee become certified as a FSSM.  (NOTE - The new manager is scheduled to take a FSSM class in the next couple of weeks.)

750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.citation_text: 750.100 - Gravy heated for breakfast today was observed wrapped for use tomorrow in the bottom holding section of the pizza cooler (gravy temp 48F-50F). Store manager stated he just talked to staff about heating only the portion needed for breakfast. Portion not heated for use is supposed to be stored in a proper container and dated for use the next day. Manager discarded the gravy in the trash. The facility is not allowed to cool/reheat gravy or any other hot foods under current medium risk classification. **Discard any heated portion of gravy that has not been used at the end of breakfast shift daily.**

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.citation_text: 750.100 - Green peppers in walkin cooler observed with significant amount of mold accumulation on the product. Manager discarded the peppers in the trash. Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750.130f - Container of flour did not have proper label. Unless the identity of a product is unmistakable, bulk foods such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name. Properly label all foods.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text: 750.130 - Packages of raw bacon were observed on the top shelf of cooler reach-in section above/next to hotdogs and lunchables. Manager relocated the bacon to the bottom shelf next to raw shell eggs. All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or away from raw foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Boxes of food  were observed on the floor in the walkin freezer. Also, lower shelves of reach-in section holding ice cream and bagged ice are not up off the ground at least 6 inches. Store all foods up off the floor, and adjust shelves so they elevate ice cream and bagged ice up off the floor at least 6 inches. Foods shall be stored properly/at least 6 inches off the floor. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750.830g - Manager could not locate quat or chlorine test strips during the inspection. Manager stated he would purchase test strips today. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) tongs hanging on shelf above 3 part sink (dried food debris); B) knife next to veggie prep sink (food debris); C) (R) drip guard of ice machine (mold); D) (R) coffee spots; E) detachable pieces inside coco & cappuccino machine; & F) back crevice of soda machine ice shoot (mold). Clean and sanitize all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 - Faucet at mopsink leaks when turned on. Get the faucet repaired so it does not leak. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - Soap was not available at back handsink across from ice machine. Manager placed soap in the dispenser during the inspection. Maintain supplies of soap and paper towels at all handsinks to allow for proper handwashing. **Employees must wash their hands before putting on gloves, between glove changes, before working with food & clean equipment, any times hands may become contaminated, and prior to bagging ice.**

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) (R) Gap was observed between the coving and floor in the women's restroom under the handsink. Men's room had the same issue last year but has been caulked. Use caulk to seal the aforementioned area in the women's room. B) Floors under/behind the ice machine and under shelving/along walls in the walkin cooler were soiled. Clean the floors as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 - A) Ceiling tiles over self service area were acoustic. Replace with smooth, cleanable tiles at the next remodel. B) Handsinks in men's room and kitchen have areas where caulk has come off and/or is starting to crack. Re-caulk the handsinks in the men's room and kitchen.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: 750.1320b - Spray bottle of bleach water in kitchen tested over 200ppm. Based on coloring of test strip (patchy black) the solution was almost pure bleach. Solution was discarded/rinsed down the 3 part sink by the manager. Toxic chemicals shall not be used in any way that may contaminate food, clean equipment/utensils, or in any way that constitutes a hazard to customers or employees. Properly use toxic chemicals.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Thermometer in ice cream freezer was broken. All cold holding units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F. Thermometer was removed from the freezer. Replace the broken thermometer with one that is in good repair. Check thermometers in all cold holding units. Make sure they are working in order to properly monitor the temperature of the units. Calibrate stem thermometers using ice water weekly/as needed.**

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Wet wiping cloth was observed on the counter above the ice cream freezer. Wet wiping cloths shall be stored in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms or if no longer needed place them in the appropriate soiled linen storage area.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) drip guard of ice machine (mold); B) coffee spout (buildup); & C) ice scoop in handsink. Wash, rinse, and sanitize the above items and all food contact surfaces (i.e. soda nozzles, ice shoot of soda machine, detachable pieces of cappuccino machine, ice scoops, etc.) between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of mold, food and other debris. Ice scoop was taken to dirty dish area to be cleaned/sanitized.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) self service area - counter below equipment, inside cabinets, & black plastic organizers; B) outside of fruit topping containers in kitchen; & C) lower section of doughnut cabinet below ledge. Clean the above items and all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 - Handsinks in both restrooms and handsink across from ice machine did not have hot water. Handsink across from ice machine was left on for ~10 minutes w/ no obvious change in water temperature. All other sinks in kitchen and the mopsink had both hot and cold water. Have a licensed plumber check/repair the handsinks in question that did not have hot water during the inspection.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - Handsink across from the ice machine had an ice scoop in it. Handsinks shall be accessible to employees at all times to allow for proper handwashing. Do not block handsinks for any reason. Ice scoop was taken to the kitchen and placed with other dirty dishes to be properly cleaned/sanitized. **Note - another ice scoop was observed stored properly in the ice machine**

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Gaps were observed between the coving and floor in both restrooms under the handsinks. Junctures between walls and floors shall be properly sealed. Fill in the areas with caulk to eliminate the gaps. B) Floor of kitchen walkin freezer had accumulation of crumbs/food debris, especially by the door/under shelves. Clean the floor in the kitchen walkin freezer. Clean all floors throughout daily/as needed, including along walls/in corners, to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 - A) Ceiling tiles above self service area were acoustic. Replace the ceiling tiles with ones that are smooth and cleanable at the next remodel. B) Piece of trim below 3 part sink was observed pulling away from the wall. Walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Properly repair or replace the trim under the 3 part sink.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: 750.1310b: Observed three bottles of transmission fluid to be stored on a shelf next to cans of Pringles, next to straws, and over a box of single-service cups. The transmission fluid was moved during inspection. Store toxic items away from or below food or single-service items.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b: Observed the nozzles on the self-service soda machine are soiled. Clean and sanitize all of the nozzles often to prevent mold growth.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: At next remodel of facility, replace the ceiling tiles above the self-service area with ceiling tiles that are non-absorbant, smooth, and easily cleanable, like those that are in the kitchen and restrooms.
